problems.problem: The learning either-or question was asked four times (10 Q2, 12 Q3, 14 Q2, 16) and the focus-scope question twice (12, 14). Uday answers only the first question, so this cost two unscripted turns (15, 17), drew impatience in his self-reports, and used up the whole pace allowance: the first FACT came at turn 10, where this script's ideal is 8.
problems.cause: 2a lists two probes but does not stop the 2b either-or motivation question being asked during 2a. 2b asks for one reply covering the reflection, the purpose numbers and the motivation, then adds two more questions (focus scope; either-or). It says nothing about order, or what to do when the either-or stays unanswered.
problems.fix: 2a: add 'Ask only these probes now; kinds of motivation wait for 2b.' 2b: add 'Put the question that blocks the next draft first. Ask an either-or question at most twice; if it is still unanswered, draft only the kinds the member confirmed and record the other as "not specified". Never ask it a third time.' Kit: k.ask warns when the same normalized question is already open twice.

problems.problem: The three numbered questions held six asks. Q1 alone asked whether the summary reads right, whether the new line replaces the old one, and whether the focus holds for the whole topic. Uday's 'yes' could not settle the either-or part, which forced the re-ask at 14.
problems.cause: 2b's single-reply template ('yes or edits to the reflection, the numbers ..., and yes or changes ...') invites yes/no framing. The focus-scope and either-or rules are appended without any limit on asks per numbered item.
problems.fix: Reply shape: 'Each numbered question asks one thing, and its example answer shows the expected form. Never put an either-or question inside a yes/no question. At most 3 asks per reply, counting every question mark.' Kit: k.check_reply counts '?' under Your turn and warns over 3.

problems.problem: Uday was asked to certify 'the purpose line in my last reply' or 'I showed earlier' without seeing it. At 28 a bracketed paraphrase stood in for the line, and at 30 he was sent back to 'the coverage table in my earlier reply'. Self-reports 25, 27 and 29 all say he had to scroll back.
problems.cause: The round-2 Certifying change ('show the full CERTIFY line once ... refer to it in one line') and the Content rule ('never repeat ... refer to it in a few words') were applied even after a long search reply came in between.
problems.fix: Certifying: 'Refer to an open CERTIFY line in one line only when it is in the immediately preceding reply and that reply had no search card or long table. Otherwise show it again, exactly, in its code block just above Your turn. Never paraphrase it.' Apply the same rule to a table the Your turn asks about.

problems.problem: The early-start reply is a wall: 3 FACT lines, then 9 tables (tags, blocks, searches, selection rule, Table 1, Table 2, coverage DRAFT, plan map) and 6 code blocks. Satisfaction fell to 2, Uday missed the strings and then asked for them, and no plain line answers his own question (is a full review worth it).
problems.cause: The Searches rule requires every source and variant in full in the same reply. Step 3 adds two review tables, the coverage DRAFT and the early-start plan map to that same reply. M9 and the 180-word cap count prose only.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'After the 1-3 FACT lines, add one plain sentence on what the reviews leave open for the focus. Show broader reviews (Table 2) as one FACT line with "show broader". Keep the coverage DRAFT to at most 5 rows.' Reply shape: 'A reply with search cards holds at most 6 tables, plan map included.'

problems.problem: k.search_report could not run, so the agent built the search display by hand (env/stir_l4_local.py, scratch/s5_compose.py). The hand-built card gave the OpenAlex search S5 no block-by-block lines or block counts, and S4's protocol block no count (M4 = 5 of 6).
problems.cause: Kit bug: search_report computes todo = [s for s in tm.get('sources', []) if str(s).lower().split()[0] ...]. With team.yaml 'sources: not given' (a string), this iterates characters, and ' '.split()[0] raises IndexError. OpenAlex was then queried with k.openalex_works directly, which gives no per-block counts.
problems.fix: Kit: src = tm.get('sources'); src = src if isinstance(src, list) else []; skip blank entries; add a solo-team test. Let run_strategy run OpenAlex blocks. Prompt Searches: 'If a helper fails, say so in one line and still give one line per block, with its count, for every source.'

problems.problem: Review Tables 1 and 2 (titles, search-end dates, paraphrased findings) carry no FACT label. The coverage DRAFT states '29 report a fat result and 10 a muscle result ... 21 name type 2 diabetes' with no inline [n]; only the 'Records examined' row cites [12]. The values are correct, but a reader cannot tie each table to its source record.
problems.cause: R2's 'one label may cover a block' does not say how to label a table. The hand-built composition (see the kit bug) added no captions or citations. Step 3 has no template for review tables.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'Caption each table of reviews "FACT, from [n]", and in a DRAFT cite [n] in every cell that uses a count.' Kit: add k.reviews_table(rows, source_ids) that emits the caption and the citations.

problems.problem: The lead FACT 'No record matched all five parts of your topic and focus (strict search, 0 records)' does not say that S1 was limited to PubMed's systematic-review subset. Just before the need decision, it can read as 'no evidence at all'.
problems.cause: The lead FACT lines were composed by hand, and the Step 3 template does not require the source and filter in the lead lines.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'In the lead FACT lines, name the source and the filter, for example "No systematic review in PubMed matched all five parts ...".' Kit: have search_report(lead=...) append the filter automatically.

problems.problem: The line 'This may change the Individual Motivation you approved, because the agreed purpose in turn shapes what each member seeks' appears right after the motivation is certified and again after the purpose. Uday found it confusing and skipped it (self-report 23).
problems.cause: R4 requires naming every certified variable a flow reaches as a possible reopening, even when the purpose only restates what the motivation already holds. The kit's trace text is generic.
problems.fix: R4: 'Name a possible reopening only when the new decision adds something the reached decision did not already assume. Otherwise say nothing, or "Your motivation still stands".' Kit: trace() suppresses the TP-to-IM note when the TP and IM records share their source answers.

problems.problem: The kit recorded 'Accepted: <full TP line>' with actor Uday at 00:32:57, 7 seconds before the line was first shown (L000061, 00:33:04), and with no refers_to. Uday had confirmed the parts (L000031, L000037) but never accepted the assembled line.
problems.cause: Kit: certify_line() reads the decision from plan.yaml, so a draft can be shown only after propose(accepted_by=<member>). That forces an acceptance record attributed to the member.
problems.fix: Kit: let certify_line(element, draft=...) show a k.draft text without any acceptance record, and set status 'proposed' at certification. Or log propose as 'Assembled from confirmed answers L000031, L000037', with actor 'agent' and refers_to those ids.

problems.problem: The optional 'When convenient' requests repeat and grow, reaching four items at 28 (email, model name, PROSPERO run, OpenAlex code). Uday calls them clutter. The PROSPERO search, which the need decision depends on, is buried among optional extras.
problems.cause: 2d prescribes the email and model-name asks, and the prompt allows optional items to be repeated. Nothing separates a registry search the step depends on from optional set-up.
problems.fix: Prompt: 'Mention each optional item once, then again only on "where are we" or in the pause summary. A registry search that a step depends on is asked for at that step's decision point, as a numbered item in Your turn, not as a When convenient item.'

judge.strengths: Fidelity is clean and checkable. Every literature number and claim at 24 traces to code over saved responses, and the review paraphrases match the saved abstracts. Certification integrity held: a bare 'Certify' was refused, the reason was asked for once and never suggested, wording equals last_shown, and each certification has a git commit. The focus was captured in Uday's own words ('what kind of weight is lost, fat or muscle') with 'Added by me: nothing', carried in the status line and the purpose line, and attributed to block 3 of the search. The agent refused at 10 to invent a focus. The status line was correct in all 13 turns, and the plan map appeared at every required event, including 'what's the next step?'. The early Step 3 start was announced, flagged in the status line and logged with its open item. The search card was thorough: field-tag key first, block counts before filters, Create Date bounds verified in the query translation, records-not-studies, unsearched sources named, and a PROSPERO string prepared with 'pending: Uday'. The 'what was the search strategy?' reply was compact, with no file pointers. Plain language was strong (no codes, rule numbers or log ids in prose), and prose stayed near the 180-word cap.
